Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the Praj Industries Limited Q2 and H1 FY 2027 
Earnings Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, 
and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes.

“*” then “0” on your touchtone phone. I now hand the conference over to Ms. Purvangi Jain

earnings conference call for the 2nd Quarter and the first half of the financial year 2027. Before 
we begin, I would like to mention a short cautionary statement. Some of the statements made 
in today's earnings con call may be forward-looking in nature. Such forward-looking statements 
are subject to risk and uncertainties, which could cause actual results to differ from those 
anticipated. Such statements are based on management's belief as well as assumptions made 
by and information currently available to the management. Auditors are cautioned not to place 
any undue reliance on these forward-looking statements in making any investment decisions. 
The purpose of today's Earnings Conference Call is purely to educate and bring awareness 
about the company's fundamental business and financial quarter under review. 
Now let me introduce you to the management participating with us in today's earnings call and 
give it over to them for their opening remarks: 
We have with us Mr. Ashish Gaikwad – Managing Director, and Mr. Sachin Raole – Joint 
Managing Director and Chief Financial Officer. 
Without any further delay, I now request Mr. Ashish Gaikwad to begin his opening remarks. 
Thank you, and over to you, sir.

Ashish Gaikwad: 
Good day, everyone. I welcome you to Praj Industries earnings call of 2nd Quarter FY 2027 and 
the First Half of FY 2027. Trust all of you had the opportunity to go through our results for the 
quarter and half year ended September 30th, 2026. 
Despite challenging environment, both domestically and in global markets, our results 
demonstrate resilience. We have delivered improved performance over the previous quarter. 
This is due to disciplined execution, increased volume, and a better mix. 
Our first-generation ethanol domestic business order booking was a mix of a few Greenfield 
and mostly Brownfield solutions. Our customers are prioritizing operational efficiency 
improvements and additional value-added co-products, such as distillers corn oil, to improve 
their plant performance and profitability. There is also a visible trend towards feedstock 
diversification. Several customers are interested to add grain modules as an add-on to their 
sugar-based plants. This gives them an ease of switching to different feedstocks based on the 
market conditions, availability, and profitability. Essentially, Praj can offer a multi-feed and a 
multi-product solution to our customers for greater business flexibility. 
Earlier this week, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has amended the Central Motor 
Vehicles Rules 1989 to legally recognize E100 or 100% ethanol as fuel for certified flex-fuel 
vehicles. We are closely monitoring the developments on this front, and this paves a way for 
ethanol capacity creation over a period of time. 
As a well-informed audience, you may know that the state-run Oil Marketing Companies, or 
OMCs, have excluded sugarcane juice, sugar syrup, and B-Heavy molasses from their recent 
ethanol procurement tenders for the 2026-2027 supply year. This leaves C-Heavy molasses 
along with approved grains like maize and broken rice as the permitted feedstock. 
As Indian ethanol producers face such feedstock variation challenges, Praj provides them the 
required operational flexibility with our proven design, decades of experience, and end-to-end 
solution and services to deal with this situation. 
On the Greenfield project backlog execution, our customers continue to experience project 
funding challenges. Ethanol supply-demand imbalance has also impacted the project backlog 
conversion to revenues. Some projects in the backlog, which were based on sugary feedstocks 
like juice, syrup, and B-Heavy molasses, are facing these challenges. We are discussing with our 
customers to find appropriate solutions, and we believe that the clarity will emerge by the end 
of this financial year. 
While Greenfield projects in domestic markets experience a slowdown, we see parts of 
international markets developing positively. These markets include the USA, Brazil, Argentina, 
Southeast Asia, and Africa. We see an opportunity pipeline of approximately INR 1,000 crores 
developing over the next few quarters.

While talking about biofuels, let me update you on the new area of establishing biofuel 
blending in diesel: We are making a steady progress on this subject. India's first bio-IBA plant, 
designed and engineered by Praj, is progressing well. The construction is expected to be 
completed by end of this year. In the meantime, various tests of bio-IBA blended in diesel on 
different diesel engines are underway. We are optimistic about this opportunity. 
Our lifecycle services business continues to grow steadily quarter-over-quarter. We have 
always shared with you in the earlier dialogue, this is one of our focus areas. We continue to 
serve our customers' installed base globally and domestically beyond the project delivery. We 
offer annual maintenance services, performance enhancers, digital plant services, spare parts, 
operations and maintenance services, and other critical services that help our customers to 
realize enhanced business benefits from their plant assets. 
Regarding our CBG business, we welcome the new GOBARdhan Policy. This policy has created 
a strong interest in the market. We see a growth in our inquiry pipeline for Napier grass, rice 
straw, and press mud-based CBG plants. I am happy to share that our board of directors has 
given us an in-principle approval to invest up to INR 100 crores via our proposed JV with BPCL 
for setting up new CBG plants. 
On front of the Sustainable Aviation Fuel, SAF, the delivery of a detailed engineering package 
for ethanol to SAF plant for an international customer is progressing well. The final investment 
decision for this project is expected in Quarter 1 of FY 2028. A favorable FID will create 
opportunities to supply equipment and modules for construction of this plant. We continue to 
pursue opportunities globally in this space, and we are ready for the prime time. 
Moving on to our engineering businesses: 
On Praj GenX business, our world-class Mangaluru facility is now approved by 18 international 
customers. We have signed four (4) framework agreements which are operationalized. These 
opportunities are for large equipment and modular projects in traditional markets like oil and 
gas, fertilizers, LNG, etc. Precision fabrication for data centers is also emerging as a growth 
opportunity in international as well as domestic markets. 
For our ZLD and PHS businesses, the conventional business is going steady. We see some new 
markets opening up and offer opportunities in the manufacturing of batteries, semiconductors, 
and solar cells. Praj has the portfolio to offer both the need for Ultra-High Purity water as well 
as the wastewater treatment with a zero liquid discharge for ZLD facility mandated by the law. 
Overall, we believe the business environment is challenging but improving. We are able to 
demonstrate the resilience and continue to invest in future businesses growth simultaneously. 
We will continue to focus on our execution rigor while leveraging new opportunities on the 
horizon.

30th, 2026:

compared to INR 8.42 billion in Quarter 2 of the last year. PBT stood at INR 361 million in

Export revenues accounted for 38%, of the total revenue69% is from Bioenergy, 21% is from 
Engineering, and 10% is from PHS business. 
The order intake during the quarter was INR 7.15 billion, with 62% from domestic and 38% 
from international. Out of the total order intake, 57% came from bioenergy, 26% from 
engineering, and balance 17% from PHS business. The order backlog as of September 2026 is 
at INR 44.6 billion, comprising of 63% of domestic orders. Cash in hand as on September 30th 
is INR 5.33 billion. 
I now conclude my remarks, and I would like to thank you all for joining us on this call. I wish 
you a very Happy Diwali in advance, and we would be now happy to discuss any questions or 
comments or suggestions you may have.
